message.content:
**Average Rent Prices in New York City (as of early‑2025)**  

| Apartment Type | Typical Monthly Rent |
|-----------------|----------------------|
| Studio          | $2,200 – $3,000      |
| One–Bedroom     | $2,800 – $4,500      |
| Two–Bedroom     | $3,600 – $6,300      |

> **Key Points**
>
> * **Neighborhood Matters:**  
>   - Manhattan’s midtown & upper‑east side studios start around **$2,400**, while luxury lofts can exceed **$7,000+.**  
>   - Brooklyn neighborhoods such as Williamsburg or Park Slope range from **$2,700** (one‑bedroom) up to **$5,500+** for larger units.  
>   - Queens (e.g., Astoria, Long Island City) offers more affordable options—studios often under **$1,900** and two‑beds below **$3,500**.  
> 
> * **Market Trends:** Rental rates fluctuate seasonally and respond strongly to economic conditions (interest rates, job growth). In late 2024, rents were still rising modestly after a brief dip during the pandemic years.  
> 
> * **Additional Costs:** Most leases include utilities (electricity, gas, water) only partially; many landlords charge separate utility bills. Some apartments offer “all‑in” packages which add roughly **$100–$250/month**.  
> 
> * **Lease Length:** Shorter lease terms (≤12 months) may carry higher monthly rates than long‑term contracts.  
> 
> * **Amenities & Building Class:** Buildings with concierge services, fitness centers, rooftop decks, or high-end finishes typically command premium rents (+10% to +30%).  
> 
> * **Rental Platforms:** Zillow, StreetEasy, Apartments.com, and local brokerages provide current listings; always verify the latest figures directly through official leasing sites or real‑estate agents.  

If you’re looking at a specific borough, zip code, or unit size, let me know—I can narrow down the estimate further!
